maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: Mr. Chairman, I should like to take up a matter which although it does not come within any of these votes is one within the jurisdiction of the Department of the Interior-I refer to the islands in James bay. The people in my section of the country do not seem to understand that these islands belong to the federal government, and I ask the minister if he has received any requests from the Ontario government to have these islands come under provincial jurisdiction. Only two years ago the natural resources were returned to the western provinces and the people in my section of the country are firmly convinced that any lands within the boundaries of James bay should come within the jurisdiction of either the government of Ontario or of Quebec. Has the minister received any correspondence, or has anything been done by the provincial governments or the federal government in the matter of giving these islands to Quebec and Ontario?

speakerposition: Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext:
If my memory serves me
correctly, I have had only one communication in regard to the jurisdiction under which these islands would come, and that is concerning one situated in Hudson bay, not in James bay. Inquiries were instituted and it was ascertained that that particular island came under the jurisdiction of Ontario rather than that of the dominion. But at the moment I recall no communication being received by the department in regard to the general question of jurisdiction and administration of those islands in James bay.

maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext:
I would infer from
the reply of the minister that any islands in the Hudson bay inland sea come under the jurisdiction of Ontario. This will naturally imply that all the islands in James bay belong to the provinces of Quebec and Ontario. I have in mind at the present time the Belcher islands, part of which, some people from Quebec contend, belong to that province. Naturally we in Ontario contend that the whole of them belong to our province. I bring up this question to emphasize the importance of knowing definitely as soon as possible under whose jurisdiction these islands come, so that there may be no delay in any improvements or work, whether mineral development or otherwise, that may be done there. The federal government and the authorities of the provinces interested, that is, Manitoba, Ontario and Quebec, should get together in the near future so as to decide the question of jurisdiction. Since the beginning of the session I have received several letters of application for certain rights, whether mining or otherwise, in some of the islands in James bay, and so far I have not been able to get any satisfactory reply from the provincial authorities. I believe at one time the minister was good enough to grant me a personal interview in which he told me the applications came under his jurisdiction. If, according to what he said a few moments ago,
!728 ^	COMMONS
Supply-Interior-Dominion Lands
the islands in Hudson, bay are really under the jurisdiction of the province of Ontario, I believe in my section of the country and even in Toronto they are unacquainted with that fact, and the government owes it to the country to make a definite statement in the matter. Their natural resources have all been given to the western provinces, and I maintain that all those islands in that great inland sea should be given to the three provinces I have mentioned. I am making this plea very earnestly on account of certain conflicts over mining and colonization laws and so forth, because if we have complication of jurisdiction, it is bound to hurt the development of that section of the country.

speakerposition: Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: I speak subject to correction, and I have not in my possession the legal opinion in respect to this matter, but as I understand it, the islands in James bay and Hudson bay proper are under the jurisdiction of the dominion parliament; that is, they belong to the crown in the right of the dominion. When I spoke about an island in Hudson bay being under the jurisdiction of the province of Ontario, I had reference to an island which is situated in the mouth of. one of the rivers. An island so situated comes under the jurisdiction of the province if the shore line on either side of the mouth of the river would, if extended, include that island in the province. I do not wish the hon. member to understand that in illustrating my point a moment ago by mentioning this particular island, I was saying that all islands in Hudson bay were under the jurisdiction of the provinces. My understanding is exactly the opposite. Any island which is situated within the bay proper, either James or Hudson bay, would belong to the crown in the right of the dominion. As I say, I speak subject to correction.

maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext:
I am indeed thankful
to the minister for the useful information he has given, but again I ask that in the near future a conference be held between the provinces interested and the federal government to decide the matter. I know from actual fact that thousands, yes, hundreds of thousands of dollars would be invested to-day in some of those James bay islands if the exact jurisdiction were known. The fact, as the minister has mentioned, that islands in the estuaries of some of the rivers are under the jurisdiction of the provinces, while islands in the Hudson and James bays are under the jurisdiction of the federal government, is the reason that people contemplating development work are afraid to go ahead with it, being in a state of uncertainty as to the matter

of jurisdiction. In making this plea I have the support of the Minister of Labour, who comes from my section of the country and is familiar with the situation. I ask the government very earnestly to band over at the earliest possible moment to the jurisdiction of the provincial governments interested1, namely, Quebec, Ontario and Manitoba, all islands within Hudson and James bays. As I have pointed out before as regards Belcher islands alone, some people maintain that part of them should belong to Quebec and part to Ontario, while naturally, as a northern Ontario man, I maintain that the whole of them should belong to Ontario. I want to impress upon the committee the fact that there are complications of this nature, and as it was an easy matter for the federal government to return the natural resources to the three western provinces, it should be easy for them to give to the provinces I have mentioned, those islands within certain degrees of latitude within Hudson and James bays. This would help wonderfully in the development of the mineral and other natural resources that require capital for development; I shall not include agriculture at the present time. This question should be settled satisfactorily so that the people may know exactly where to file their applications. When there are legal complications between the provincial and the federal authorities people naturally are not willing to spend their money. The mining laws of the dominion differ in some respects from those of Ontario, and on that score alone I would urge upon the minister the necessity of calling such a conference. I know the government in the near future will receive communications from people interested in the development of northern Ontario, strongly urging that this matter be settled at an early date.

speakerposition: Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext:
I shall be very glad to
give consideration to the representations made by the hon. member.

maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext:
In respect of the first item dealing with seed grain relief, I understand in those cases the liens are taken on the land itself. I have two or three questions to ask in that regard and I think I can put them together. The minister can consider and answer them after I have finished. First, do those seed grain liens, nominally at least, still carry interest? Second, is there any large number of these old seed grain liens within that part of Saskatchewan which has suffered from crop failures for some years and is now receiving one hundred per cent relief? Third,

Supply-Interior-Dominion Lands
if so, which of these two liens-the old seed grain lien upon the land or the new lien upon the crop in connection with which notes have been given payable to the Saskatchewan Relief Commission-has priority? Perhaps I need not ask the fourth question, for an estimate by the minister as to the value of either the old liens in that district or of the new notes recently signed. But the first three questions are serious.

speakerposition: Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: In reply to the first question, interest is being charged on the old liens. In reply to the second, whether some of these liens are still existent in the southern part of Saskatchewan in the dried out areas, although I cannot answer categorically, but speaking from my experience in dealing with the matter I would say that these liens are attached to lands in all parts of Saskatchewan as well as to lands in Manitoba and Alberta. As to the question which lien would have priority, the old seed grain which was put on the land or the new lien in Saskatchewan which was put on the crop, I would say, although I am not a lawyer, that the old lien would come first because it was put on the land. That lien would have priority over all other charges against that land, especially in those cases where relief was granted fifty per cent by the dominion and fifty per cent by the province. Although the legal members of the house may be in a better position to answer that question than I am, my own opinion is that the first lien would have priority.

maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: May I ask the minister if he is right in his contention that - there is still some money owing by the farmers of Manitoba to the federal government on account of seed grain advances in 1914-15? I am under the impression that Manitoba does not owe anything to the federal government for that advance of seed grain. Am I right in that or not?

speakerposition: Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: I think the hon. member is quite correct when he states that there is nothing owing to the Dominion government for seed grain advances in the year 1914-15. But I did not understand him to refer particularly to 1914-15 when he asked his first question. There is money owing to the Dominion government for seed grain and fodder relief in the province of Manitoba, but not for 1914-15. It goes back as far as the year 1876, when there was a grasshopper plague in Manitoba, and some of the liens given at that time have not yet been discharged.

maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: I cannot believe that the minister is serious in saying that the farmers of Manitoba-I am speaking of the farmers -owe anything to the federal government on account of seed grain relief in 1876. Was not that all wiped out some years ago?

speakerposition: Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: No, it was not.

maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: Does the government intend to try to collect that money?

maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: Is that what Mr. Drew is doing, trying to collect money advanced in 1876?

speakerposition: Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: He is trying not only to collect but also to adjust.

maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: I think this is a most ridiculous situation which has been presented to the house. Imagine keeping a man in Winnipeg to collect money advanced to settlers back in the year 1876, most of whom are probably dead by this time. Before this item passes we ought to get details of these advances; the committee should be told just how much of this money has been collected in recent years and What Mr. Drew is doing in Manitoba in that regard. Really it is a most ridiculous situation.

speakerposition: Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext:
It is a situation which
has been before this house practically every year since then.

maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: But it has not been presented as plainly as now.

speakerposition: Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext:
I was not minister in
previous years. As I said, Mr. Drew is not simply endeavouring to collect, because I am quite as well aware as the hon. member of the inability of the farmers of Manitoba to pay under present conditions. Mr. Drew is endeavouring to adjust these matters. Recommendations come forward at frequent intervals from Mr. Drew, with whom is associated an official of the provincial government, and in a great many instances his recommendations have been that these seed grain liens be cancelled. But they are not cancelled until the matter has been investigated and the recommendation forwarded by the commissioner.

maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: What commissioner?

speakerposition: Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext:
Mr. Drew, with whom is
associated an official of the provincial government, by the name, I think, of Mr. Gyles.

maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: They adjust these seed advances?

speakerposition: Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext:
Yes, seed grain and fodder relief.



Supply-Interior-Dominion Lands

maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: The only seed grain involved in this discussion goes back as far as 1876. Am I not right in that?

speakerposition: Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext:
I do not think that is
quite correct.

maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext:
That was the statement
we got from the minister.

speakerposition: Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext:
No, some go back as far
as 1876, but advances for seed grain and fodder relief have also been made in the intervening years. I cannot give the hon. member the details, as I have not got them here.

maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: I think we had better have the details. The very fact that the minister has mentioned 1876 indicates that it is a situation that needs to be investigated. Those old liens, of course, should be cancelled at once. The item had better stand until we get the details.

speakerposition: Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: If it will suit the purpose of the hon. member I shall be very glad to furnish him with a statement showing the advances that have been made over the different years and the amount collected.

maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: For the information of the hon. member for Red Deer, who asked the minister which of the two liens would have priority, may I say that the liens that are being taken to-day for seed grain advanced in Saskatchewan are not being placed against the land, but against the crop, due on August 14, 1932.

maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext:
I am quite familiar
with that fact, but I wondered whether a lien against the land itself might also include a lien on the crop grown on the land, in which case, of course, it would take priority.

maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext:
Do I understand that
if we allow this item to pass the minister will bring down the information we desire to have about Manitoba?

speakerposition: Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext:
Certainly, I shall be very
glad to do so.

maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: We would like to know when these advances for seed grain and fodder were made to the farmers of Manitoba, the amount advanced and the amount repaid, together with the amount of the interest.

maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext:
I would like to know the
amount repaid year by year.

maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: And how much damage the grasshoppers did in 1876, if the minister has that information.

maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext:
I notice that this item
speaks of admiralty and public lands. What is that?

speakerposition: Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext:
The Department of the
Interior, as the hon. member is aware, has for many years administered the dominion lands. From time to time ordnance lands have been turned over to the Department of the Interior from the Department of National Defence, when that department no longer had use for the lands for their particular purposes.

speakerposition: stagedirection
speechtext:
Item agreed to.
To assist in publishing the transactions of the Association of Dominion Land Surveyors, $125.

maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext:
What is this amount
voted for?

maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: Will the minister explain the term "publishing the transactions"?

speakerposition: Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext:
The sum of $125 is asked
for the purpose of assisting the Association of Dominion Land Surveyors in the publishing of their annual report. Not only will this grant aid the association in the publication of papers read at their annual meeting, but it will enable them to employ the services of a shorthand reporter so that the discussion following the reading of papers may be available. The report contains information of great value to the general public, as well as to officers in the government whose duties are connected with surveying and engineering.

speakerposition: stagedirection
speechtext:
Item agreed to.
Advancement of forest conservation in Canada, $254,000.

maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext:
Does the administration of
the nursery at Indian Head come under this vote?

speakerposition: Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext:
The nurseries at Indian
Head and Sutherland are now administered by the Department of Agriculture.

maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext:
Owing to the fact that
this is an item involving an expenditure of $254,000 I should like to know in what provinces and to what extent the advancement of forest conservation is being carried out?

speakerposition: Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext:
This item covers not only the advancement of forest conservation but also the total contribution made by the Dominion government towards the technical research into forest products. The description of this vote is hardly accurate; it covers the total amount set aside by parliament for the purpose of carrying on technical investigations into forestry matters throughout the dominion.

Supply-Interior-Forestry

maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: Does reforestation come under this item?

speakerposition: Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: No.

maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext:
Why is there such a large
decrease in the vote?

speakerposition: Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: The decrease comes about simply through the general policy of economy.

maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: In what way have decreases been made?

speakerposition: Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext:
The forestry department
maintain three laboratories, one at Ottawa, one at Montreal, and one at Vancouver. The services carried on in Ottawa are of a purely technical nature, dealing with such subjects as wood utilization, the study of the application of fire retardants to wood or wood material, and the increasing uses to which wood may be put. In the Montreal laboratory the work is solely for the purpose of assisting Canadian pulp and paper industries. The one in Vancouver concerns itself with the utilization of British Columbia woods. In addition to that the general services rendered by the forestry department are made available so that cooperative action may be taken with the provinces in compiling information as to the forest resources of Canada.

maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext:
Is there a decrease in all
these services?

speakerposition: Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: There is a decrease in all these activities. Although the services are being maintained, less service is being given in the department.

maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: I understood the minister to say that the work of reforestation, the management of forestry branches at different points and the practice of providing seedlings and young trees to farmers had been taken over by the Department of Agriculture?

speakerposition: Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: I said that the nursery stations at Indian Head and Sutherland were being administered by the Department of Agriculture. There are other stations, however, of a different nature, where different problems in forestry are studied, and which are still administered by the forestry department.

maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: That was my understanding. I understand that the practice of distributing seedlings and young trees is now carried on by the Department of Agriculture, but the nurseries of another type where technical work is carried on and where a study is made of the utilization of different woods are still under the jurisdiction of the Department of the Interior.

speakerposition: Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext:
That is correct.
41761-109J

maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: I think I am voicing the opinion of all farmers when I say we were greatly relieved when we learned that the work of reforestation and of handling nurseries and the distribution of seedlings and young trees throughout the farms on the bald prairies had not been done away with. About a year ago we were shocked to learn that there was a possibility of this service being discontinued, and we are now delighted to know that it is still being carried on. Coming from a prairie province, the minister will be as familiar as the rest of us with the splendid work done in the past by the department he now heads, and the great loss which would be suffered if that work were discontinued.

maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: I understood the minister to say that this grant covers several activities, such as forestry research, fire protection and so on. How is the money allocated to each activity?

speakerposition: Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: The estimates for 1932-33 are as follows: Head office administration, $25,290; research and investigation, $29,352; Petawawa experimental station, $20,033; research and investigations, $15,532; prairie district, main and suboffices, $8,893; research and investigations, $21,374; British Columbia, district offices, research and investigations, $15,353; forest product laboratories at Ottawa, $60,080; Montreal, $32,589; Vancouver, $25,504; giving a total as shown in the item of $254,000.

maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: Does not the aerial forest patrol come under this item, or has the service been discontinued?

speakerposition: Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: Now that each province has control of its own resources the forest patrol and fire protection service is a provincial activity.

maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: Did the forest patrol come under this item before, and would it represent the $146,000 decrease?

speakerposition: Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: Before the natural resources passed to the western provinces the Dominion government did maintain the patrol service under this item. But I do not desire the hon. member to be under any misunderstanding, for of course he realizes that the natural resources were transferred in 1930, and therefore there was nothing included in the estimates last session for fire patrol work.

maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext:
Does this grant include an appropriation for advertising of fire protection?
Supply-Interior

speakerposition: Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: No, there is nothing in this item for that purpose.

maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: I am doubtful, Mr. Chairman, of the advisability of the government making the change they did with respect to the forestry stations at Indian Head and Sutherland. In the opinion of the minister will this service be performed more cheaply than it was done under the forestry department by men who were especially trained for that kind of work? Everyone knows that the forestry patrol stations under the Department of the Interior had the approbation of every individual interested in tree planting. Now that this work is relegated to a secondary position I have very grave doubts as to the wisdom of the transfer. I am bound to say that I think the tree planting stations would be much better administered under the Department of the Interior.

speakerposition: Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: I aim sorry I have no actual figures to give the committee as to the savings which it was hoped might be made by the transfer of these stations from the Department of the Interior to the Department of Agriculture; but doubtless the Minister of Agriculture (Mr. Weir) will be able to give the information, or I shall be pleased to obtain it for the hon. member.

maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: How many inspectors were dispensed with by reason of the transfer?

speakerposition: Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: Speaking from memory, I think we had nine inspectors doing this in-speotional work.

maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: Not continuously?

speakerposition: Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: No; at periods of the year some of their work was carried on at the forestry stations. I think I am correct in stating that three of those men have been retained by the Department of Agriculture for inspectional purposes.

maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext:
In reply to the last
question I asked him the minister stated that his department did not now maintain an aerial forestry patrol service. In what manner are the national parks patrolled?

speakerposition: Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: The patrolling is done for us by the national defence department.

maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext:
With regard to the
forests products laboratory, I note $60,000 is provided for Ottawa; $32,000 for Montreal; and $25,000 for Vancouver. Would it not be better to have one central forest products

laboratory so that effective work might be done in testing woods and finding new uses to which they can be put? One of the serious handicaps that the forest products business of this country labours under is that through lack of such research work we find it difficult to meet world competition. For example, in the British market we cannot meet competition from Norway and Sweden and other European countries because up to the present time we have not gone far enough in practical tests of different classes of Canadian woods to be able to say to the British importers just what purpose any particular class of wood will serve. Up to date the whole scheme of laboratory work so far as forest products are concerned has been wholly inadequate. I understand this vote has been reduced, and when it is spread over three laboratories it seems to me that we are simply maintaining a skeleton organization that serves no useful purpose. Instead, we should be furthering the interests of the forest products business of this country by more intensive research work. I believe that if the laboratory experts were brought here they would tell us that, were their work concentrated in one place, they could carry on more efficiently than when they are spread out as they are now.

maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext:

I do not blame the minister for the delay which has taken place in this matter, but surely, when practically all the rest of the international obligations have been adjusted in that neck of the woods, as we call it, the settlers should not be the only ones not taken care of. Settlement has been made of the

Supply-Interior-National Parks
question as to what height of water shall be maintained in the lake of the Woods, and, if I remember rightly, the International Joint Commission recommended in 1916 that compensation should be made for lands destroyed or flooded. I have personal knowledge of many settlers who have been flooded out by the Winnipeg river. I understand that the province of Ontario says that it has nothing to do with this matter. I have not before me a copy of the votes and proceedings of the Ontario legislature, but mj' information is that the Minister of Mines gave an answer to a question on the floor of the provincial house to the effect that the legal authorities had said that the province was not legally bound to pay. I am not sure whether our Department of Justice has made a similar ruling, but if these payments are to be based on the elimination of technicalities, the settlers will never be compensated. The Naims are based not upon technicalities but upon the findings and recommendations of the International Joint Commission. Lands have been flooded and homes destroyed, and in view of the fact that this government has more to do with the International Joint Commission than the provincial government, I think it Should see that these settlers are taken care of at as early a date as possible.

maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: Is any portion of this amount for historic sites earmarked for repairing Port Prince of Wales at the mouth of the Churchill river in northern Manitoba? The minister paid a visit to that fort along with myself and several others last year, and as I stated to him at that time there is more history and more tragedy woven around that fort than any other historic site in Canada. It was built by the Hudson's Bay Company from 1733 to 1741 at the time the English and French were at grips in the bay for the fur trade. The fort is about three hundred feet square, built of solid stone masonry, with walls from thirty t6 forty feet thick, and there are about forty very large guns scattered around the ramparts and now lying buried in the mud. The fort is rapidly falling apart. The arch of the main door is falling down and is held up only by a stick of timber placed there through the kindness of some official of the Department of Railways and Canals. This year a great many people will be visiting Churchill because the eyes of the whole world are focussed upon this new port, and it certainly is a disgrace that this historic fort should be allowed to remain in its present state. I hope that the minister will use his best endeavours to have at least a small amount of money spent this year to set up and reinforce the main gateway, dig the guns out of the mud, and generally make this historic site a little more presentable.

To provide for a refund of amount paid in 1928 on behalf of the Central Manitoba Mines Limited, being royalty on gold obtained from mineral claims in the province of Manitoba and acquired under the provisions of the Quartz Mining regulations, $1,916.37.

maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: I think we should have some explanation on that item. Why are these people being paid the sum of money mentioned?

speakerposition: Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext:
The Yukon Quartz and
Yukon Placer Mining Acts, applicable to that territory only, as well as quartz mining regulations applicable to the prairie provinces and the Northwest Territories, provided for the payment to the crown of a royalty on gold at the rate of 37J cents per ounce. On June 11, 1928, the Yukon Quartz Mining Act was amended to provide for the payment of a royalty on the profits of the mine in excess of 110,000 during any year, in lieu of a fixed royalty of 371 cents per ounce, but the royalty on placer gold remained unchanged. It was understood that a similar amendment would be made as soon as possible to the quartz mining regulations applicable to the prairie provinces, but as a general revision and amendment of these regulations was at the time engaging the attention of an interdepartmental committee, the change referred to was not made effective until April 1, 1929- that is, for a period of nine months thereafter. During that time Central Manitoba Mines, Limited, paid in royalties the sum of $1,916.37, which was at a higher rate than afterwards obtaining, and for that reason they are asking for a refund.

To provide for expenses in connection with determination of location and boundaries of ordnance and admiralty lands in the province of British Columbia, $3,000.

maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext:
Would the minister kindly
explain this item?

speakerposition: Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext:
Section 8 of the agreement of February 20, 1930, between the dominion and the province of British Columbia on the transfer of the railway belt and Peace river block, provides for the appointment of two persons, one by the governor general in council and one by the lieutenant-governor in council, to determine the location and boundaries of the several parcels of ordnance and admiralty lands within and without the railway belt. By section 6 of

Supply-Lnterior
the said agreement, ordnance and admiralty lands included in the railway belt did not pass to the province. By section 7 of the said agreement, all ordnance and admiralty lands which were set aside as such before 1871, and which have been transferred to Canada by the Imperial government, continue to be vested in and administered by the government of Canada. It is provided, however, that Canada shall recognize and confirm any alienation of any part of such lands made by the province prior to the date of the said agreement. The dominion also undertakes to perform every obligation of the province under any agreement made by the province or any provincial act, orders in council or regulation.
It is very advisable at the earliest possible date there should be a dear understanding with the province as to the location and boundaries of the several parcels of ordnance and admiralty lands in the province of British Columbia, some of which are said to be very valuable. It is therefore proposed to provide a sum of $3,000 for the expenses of a commissioner to be appointed under the authority of section 8, who will possibly be accompanied by a departmental expert, as the matter of titles to be investigated is in some cases very complicated.

maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: I have lived in western Canada for twenty-six years and I am puzzled to know what are admiralty lands.

speakerposition: Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: In the main they are lands which were set aside by the British Admiralty in the early days for admiralty purposes. They have been transferred to the crown in the right of the dominion.

maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext:
What were those admiralty
purposes?

speakerposition: Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: I am sorry my knowledge of history is not sufficient to inform the hon. member for what particular purpose any parcel of land was set aside, but as I understand it, these parcels of land were set aside for various admiralty purposes in the same manner that ordnance lands are set aside for military purposes.

To provide amounts required for expropriation of areas for right of way on the Savona-Port Moody section of the main line of the Canadian Pacific Railway, also on the Pembina and Stonewall branches of the same road, $2,500.

maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: Explain.

speakerposition: Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext:
In connection with those
portions of the Canadian Pacific Railway
which were constructed by the Dominion government and afterwards turned over to the Canadian Pacific Railway Company, it is provided in the contract between the dominion and the company that the necessary right of way for the railway will be acquired by the government where necessary. Before this department had advice as to what lands were affected by the right of way, a certain number of patents were issued which contained no reservation of the lands required for the railway. Many years ago the neccessary deeds were obtained from owners in a large number of cases, but some cases have remained unsettled up to the present time. The areas in each case are small, but in addition to paying for the land the government has to provide the necessary expenses for the legal work connected with the transfer of title. It is impossible to forecast what expenditure may be required, as there is no means of knowing what price will be demanded by the various owners, nor is there any means to estimate what amount will be required for legal purposes, and possibly for expropriation proceedings. The sum of $2,500 is named merely as affording a basis for action to clear off all these pending cases as far as possible in 1932-33. The Department of Justice has advised that it is the duty of the Dominion government to procure title for the railway in all these cases.

maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext:
There are one or two matters I should like to bring to the attention of the minister. The treaty was entered into in 1916 and will expire this fall, but it is provided that it shall remain in force from year to year after that date or until notice is given by either party to determine it. The people of Prince Edward Island think that our American friends have been getting the best of the bargain, and that we are really preserving the birds in the maritimes for their benefit- Two or three years in succession the provincial legislature has passed a resolution objecting to the renewal of the treaty without the province being consulted. One recital in the resolution states:
Supply-Interior

Whereas the said prohibition was enacted without receiving the assent of the government or the legislative assembly of the province of Prince Edward Island.
They refused to be a party to the treaty. Another recital states:
And whereas the government of the province was requested to enact a law confirming the provision of the said treaty and the federal legislation thereunder, which the government refused to do.
The government of Prince Edward Island has absolutely refused to be a party to this legislation. As the treaty expires this year, would the minister consult the three maritime provinces, particularly Prince Edward Island, to find out just what their objections are? Perhaps he could give us some information regarding the proposal he has in mind for continuing the treaty.

speakerposition: Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: I am not in a position to state that the provisions of this treaty are satisfactory in their entirety to any or all of the provinces. I think the hon. member will realize the difficulties that any government would be under in drafting a treaty or formulating regulations under it which would be satisfactory to each province. But I may say for his information that the provinces have-been consulted in regard to the operations of this treaty, officers of this department being continually in touch with officials of the various game departments of the provinces. As for over twenty-five years I have been a sportsman myself, I feel I have some little knowledge with regard to this problem. I am quite convinced of the value of the treaty to the people of Canada and to Canadian sportsmen. From my knowledge of its workings I believe it is very important not only from that standpoint, but by reason of the provisions it contains for the protection of insectivorous birds. The hon. member knows that increasingly our crops, both grain and vegetable as well as fruit, have been suffering from the ravages of insects, and it is most important that we protect our bird life, especially the insectivorous birds. That protection is one of the main items in the treaty and I do not at present intend to take any step to discontinue the treaty, although I do not say that regulations drafted thereunder might not be amended from time to time to suit particular areas in different parts of the country.

Mr. MaeINNIS: I wish to call to the attention of the minister certain matters in connection with the Migratory Birds Convention Act, and in doing so I may say that I am speaking not from personal knowledge but from what has been told me. The licences or permits given to collectors in British Columbia for the collection of specimens have been, I am informed, largely abused. I am encouraged to bring this to the attention of the minister in view of his reply to the question asked by the hon. member for Prince and the minister's intimation that he realizes the value of conserving the bird life of Canada for the good of the country. I am informed that there are really too many licences or permits granted for the collection of specimens, and that the specimens collected are indeed the rarest birds. It is stated that the number of specimens allowed each collector is far too great, and that the privilege of collection has been commercialized. Furthermore, it is pointed out that collectors coming in from other countries, particularly the United States, are allowed to collect specimens without any restriction whatsoever:	That there is a certain amount of
commercialization can be substantiated by the case tried in the British Columbia courts recently. The person prosecuted claimed that he was merely exchanging skins of one kind for skins of another, and the magistrate held that an exchange of that kind was tantamount to a sale of skins outright. I had some definite information on the subject, but not knowing that this question would come up to-night I did not bring it with me; I cannot therefore present it to the minister at the moment. If, however, he wishes, I shall be glad to give him the names of those who have complained to me and to help him in any way I can.

Is the hon. member
asking the question in connection with the appropriation, or is it a different question he is asking now?

maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: My question is based on the vote.

maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext:
If the
minister will look at page 10 of his annual report he will find the following: Between March 31, 1930, and the end of 1931, there were new pensions awarded by the Board of 
Pension Commissioners, 4,394 for disability and 1,473 for dependent pensioners, and new pensions awarded by the pension tribunal and pension appeal court, 405 for disability and 52 for dependent pensioners. That is apart from the final payments. I think the question my hon. friend was trying to frame was: What is the estimate this year by way of new pensions to be awarded, in the first place by the Board of Pension Commissioners, and in the second place by the pension tribunal and the pension appeal court?

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext:
As I was saying, there
are 2,000 of those for final payment. I cannot give the number estimated for the others, except that it is based on the number passing through from month to month.

maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext:
That is
a point I want to emphasize. There is no disposition, is there, on the part of the department gradually to lower the estimate of the number of cases for next year that will be granted pensions? In other words, there is no tendency to be more strict in the adjudication?

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: No; on the contrary we are anticipating an increase, not a diminution in the pensions. There will probably be an increase in pensions for some considerable time.

maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext:
If the minister says
they are anticipating an increase in applications for pensions, why the decrease in the estimate?

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext:
Evidently I have failed
to make the matter clear. Although there is a decrease in the actual estimate, it will allow $4,000,000 more this year than was spent last year on pensions.

maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext:
Perhaps
if the minister will give the increase last year over the year previous and then the estimated increase this year over last year, we shall see whether there is a progressive increase or not.

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE

speakerposition: stagedirection
speechtext:
Item agreed to.

maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext:
Would
the minister be good enough to inform the committee as to the success of the amendment of last year in regard to the Board of Pension Commissioners themselves dealing in the first place with all applications for pension?

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: That is a question I have much more satisfaction in answering than many others coming under pensions, because the effect of the amendment passed last year was really good. There was a very decided effect on the administration as regards applicants. I should like to put the following on record for the information of the committee: applications for pension received by the Board of Pension Commissions from August 1, 1931, to February 29, 1932, amounted in all to 14,347. Applications granted during the same period numbered: 7,084. That, I think, was a large number within that period. While there have been many cases where the progress in granting pensions has been slow and has taken fnuch time, here is one instance where a large number of applications have been dealt with and1 pensions granted within a comparatively short time. That is one of the very gratifying results of the amendments passed last year. In addition, the pension board had 2,150 applicants medically examined. The board has still a large number of cases to deal with.

maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: Is it not a fact that the amendments of last year throwing this work on the pension board have lessened the work of the tribunals out in the country?

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: They have lessened it materially, for two reasons. They actually deal with the cases themselves, and many of them finally. In addition, the work has been pushed back, as it were, to the pension board, and some of these cases, of course, will ultimately come to the tribunal.

maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: In round figures some 14,000 applications came before the board, and of these some 7,000 were accepted and pensions granted. How many of the balance either were referred to the tribunal or made application to the tribunal?

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: I have not the exact figures on that, but the pension board was required to assign reasons in writing for declining a pension, and at the same time to inform the applicant that if he could get additional evidence his case would be reconsidered, and if that additional evidence was not satisfactory he could still ask for a hearing before the tribunal. So far many of the applicants whose claims have not been granted have rested there, but they still have the right, which they may ultimately exercise, to proceed further, as I have just stated. The fact remains that a large proportion of those who have not had their claims granted have not proceeded further. I am told that about 500 of the 7,000 have asked for a hearing before the tribunal.

maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: That is 500 out of the 7,000 who were not granted a pension?

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext:
Exactly. There were about
7,000	granted and 7,000 declined, so it was about fifty-fifty.

maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: What became of the 7.000 cases in which a pension was declined? The minister will see my point. What is clogging the machinery? Is it because of the great number of applications that are being heard? The minister says that 500 of these 7,000 who were not granted a pension are asking for a hearing before the tribunal. What became of the others?

maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: He has just told you.

maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext:
He has not, and with all
respect to my hon. friend from South Toronto, the minister can handle his estimates without his assistance.

maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: I am only addressing myself to my hon. friend, not to the minister.

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext:
I cannot say what has
become of the others. All I can say is that they have not proceeded further. They were informed that their application was not granted and they were given the reasons why it was not granted. They were told that they had the opportunity to collect further evidence and to have their case reviewed by the same board, and if an unfavourable decision were then given, they had still the opportunity of being heard before the tribunal. There were about seven thousand of them, ' of whom five hundred have asked to be heard before the tribunal. What about the rest? I do not know. They have not signified anything. They may be looking for further evidence, and they may still ask to be heard before the tribunal. We do not know anything except that they have been so informed, and that with the exception of about five hundred they have not proceeded further.

maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext:
With all respect to the minister I can scarcely credit that statement that only some five hundred of
Supply-Pensions

the seven thousand whose applications were not accepted by the Board of Pension Commissioners are not proceeding further before the pension tribunal or the appeal court, because in reply to a question on the seventeenth day of February the minister replied to me that there were pending at that date, which was just the other day practically, 2,436 cases before the pension tribunals, and before the appeal court 1,231 cases. If the minister's statement is correct the majority of these cases now pending must have antedated the amendment of last year.

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: Yes, they are not included in the 14,000 to which I was referring.

maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: I would like to ask a question on a point of procedure. Where cases come before the tribunal and are adjudicated upon, whether favourably or unfavourably to an applicant, what then is the policy of the administration as to the appeal }f such cases? Is there any general instruction that all cases favourable to the applicant shall be appealed?

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: I do not think there is any policy. It is all laid down in the Pension Act. I understand that the question is, in the event of a case failing before the tribunal-

maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: In the event of a case being adjudicated upon favourably to the applicant, is it automatically appealed?

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext:
No, certainly not. In
the event of an applicant succeeding or failing before the tribunal, the procedure is not a matter of policy at all. It is all laid down in the act. The pensions advocate has the right of appeal for the applicant, and the commission counsel has the right of appeal on behalf of the pension board.

maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext:
The significance of the figures is that whereas since their inception there were 4,545 cases referred to the pension tribunals, of which number they allowed 2,129 and disallowed 2,416-about a fifty fifty proportion-there were appealed by the pension applicants 1,172 and by the commission counsel, who is ostensibly representing the administration or the treasury, 1,550. So that the commission counsel, whether under instructions or not, has appealed far more cases than have advocates acting on behalf of soldiers applying for pensions. I asked' the question how many decisions rendered by the appeal court were in favour of the applicants? The reply was:
On appeals by pension applicants, 26; by commission counsel, 239.

Almost ten to one of the appeals sent to the appeal court were in favour of appeals lodged by commission counsel as against those lodged by pension advocates. Then I asked the question:
How many were adverse to the pension applicant?
And received the answer:
On appeals by pension applicants 703, by commission counsel 343.
Taking it in a negative way we find on appeals there were far fewer decisions against commission counsel than there were against applicants for pensions. I think the figures speak for themselves with relentless severity.
I recall that last year during a discussion on the estimates it was pointed out that a circular letter under date of June 25, 1931 had been sent out by the chief commission counsel to all commission counsel throughout Canada instructing them to pursue the most rigid course in regard to these appeals. On that occasion I complimented the minister because the minute the matter came to his attention he was good enough to withdraw that letter from circulation. I trust there are no more* instructions of that type being given to commission counsel. Speaking for myse'lf I have the utmost confidence in the personnel of the tribunals; I think they have done a remarkable work, but I have very little confidence in the attitude of the appeal court, as constituted, towards the claims of the applicants.

maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: I should like to say to the minister that I am not criticizing him; I have found him friendly and considerate, and he has gone out of his way on several occasions personally to investigate oases concerning pensions I have brought to his attention. Therefore anything I may have to say is not critical of the minister. It appears to me, however, that he must realize by now that the Pension Act, with the amendments which were added in 1930, is far from being .perfect, I should like to ask if it is the intention of the government at this session to bring down any amendment or amendments to the act.

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext:
I should like to say a few words concerning several points brought up by hon. members opposite. In the first place, it is the right of applicants to appeal. All they have to do is to advise or request a pension advocate to have it done. That is a matter entirely apart from the department. Then, appeals by commission counsel are not departmental matters. Commission counsel acting under the Board of Pension Commissioners make the appeals which in their judgment should be made. I should not like to

Supply-Pensions
agree with the remarks of the hon. member for Vancouver Centre about the appeal court.
I have had much to impress me concerning the good work done by that court. There are certain facts we must bear in mind concerning the three courts. The Board of Pension Commissioners, or some of them, have been acting for ten years or more. They are well trained, experienced men. At the head of the appeal court is a man who was on the supreme court bench of one of the provinces for about fifteen years, a man who has had an extensive training and is fitted for his position. Then there is the tribunal composed of twelve members chosen from every portion of the dominion and representing the different provinces. Naturally most of those men have not been trained in their particular work; they are new men at new work, and I think it is fair to expect that some time will elapse before they learn accurately the value of evidence. I should like hon. members to bear in mind that I recognize there is a marked disparity between the number of appeals allowed on applications by advocates and by commission counsel. I am not going to judge these officials harshly because I think they are all trying to do their best. We may reasonably suppose it will take time to train men properly to weigh evidence as it should and will be done.

maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: I should like to straighten out a matter of procedure. Did I understand the minister to say that the Board of Pension Commissioners instructs the appeals on behalf of the crown, so to speak?

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: So that each case is considered by the Board of Pension Commissioners, and it is the board which gives the instructions that the appeal be taken?

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: I understood the commission counsel-

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: Yes, that is true; the chief commission counsel is an official of the pension board.

maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext:
It did transpire last year that a circular letter was sent out which provoked a good many appeals-at least that was the inference. The minister was good enough to see that that letter was withdrawn. Perhaps the minister will let us know if within his knowledge any active part has been taken in invoking the appeal to the federal appeal board since that time, because there is a feeling on the part of some that the right of 41761-110
appeal by commission counsel has been very largely used. In many cases that appeal has been successful, whereas the appeal by the man has not been successful to anything like the same extent. I should like to be assured that it is not departmental policy that there should be such a large proportion of appeals by the commission counsel against the tribunal decisions.

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: As I have just stated, it is not departmental policy. As soon as my attention was drawn to the letter sent out last year I disapproved of it and asked the pension board to recall it. The chief counsel is an official of the pension board.

maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: It does appear to me that the great defect of the Pension Act is the delay in dealing with cases that come before the tribunals. I have personal knowledge of twenty cases, of which ten or twelve have been pending for eight, nine, ten and twelve months, and two cases have been pending for fifteen months.

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: I cannot discuss specific cases-

maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: I would not expect the minister to do that.

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext:
I have found that so many conditions were supposed to exist, but a close analysis threw a different light on them.
I do not know whether those cases are still pending, but the applicants sometimes delay their own cases. As to legislation this session, the question is being very closely studied at the present time. Of course, delay cannot be wholly avoided. We are aware now what this machinery is costing the country, and surely no one is going to advocate that it be increased still further. We are trying to expedite the work as far as possible, but, as I pointed out, the pension board is granting more cases than the tribunal and the appeal court hear.

maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: I would not suggest for a moment that the machinery be increased, but could not the present machinery be speeded up? For instance, the tribunals meet at certain points in Ontario, but although there, may be twelve or fourteen cases on the docket they will sit for a day, dispose of four or six cases, and then move on to another point. Would it not be possible for the tribunal to clear the docket before they moved on?

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext:
If any hon. member will look over the itinerary he will find that the tribunals do clear the docket in each place.

Supply-Interior-Indians

In Toronto we have had a board sitting continuously for the last few months. In many centres the tribunals sit for three, four or five days and dispose of their work.

maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext:
That may apply to
Toronto, but let me take Stratford in the county where the tribunal meets. To my knowledge that tribunal has never sat longer than a day and a half although there would be twelve or fourteen cases on the docket. In that time it could deal with only four or six cases. Why should not the docket be cleared before the tribunal moves on to another point?

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: There is no reason why the tribunal should not do so.

maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: "Will the minister look into that?

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: I will ask that an itinerary be sent to the hon. member which will show how long the tribunals have sat in the different centres during the last six months.

maintopic: SUPPLY-CANADIAN CURRENCY STATEMENT OF MR. COOTE ON MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext:
We have succeeded in getting the tribunal to sit in Sherbrooke once. There were fifteen cases on the docket. The tribunal spent only one day there, heard five cases, and then moved on to another centre, just as the hon. member for South Perth (Mr. Sanderson) had said. Of the five cases heard two were immediately dismissed and in the other three the applicants were granted extensions of pensions. But those three cases were appealed, and not a thing was done for any of the applicants. One of those is the most glaring case I have had anything to dp with. It is an absolute shame. If I were to make any suggestion it would be that the decisions of these tribunals be final.
Item stands.
